detail.longDescription:
I’ve been working on this with Claude for hours now. I’m looking for security
audits, programming advice, etc. It’s a global git repository bulletin board
(Reddit with P2P support) system. Users merge the repo with each other as they
encounter one another. You only follow heads from people you know. Conversations
are merged with anyone in the conversation. And you don’t propagate content from
users you’ve blocked. And, unlike other projects of this nature, old
conversations do fall off the network (Briar and Manyverse both refused this and
their users ended up getting databases that were huge. Briar relied on SQLite,
which frequently became corrupted and lost everything, even the user’s
identity). This uses git directory storage. The only thing it lacks is image
support, so users can’t spam the network with huge files. Since anything
generated by AI cannot hold a copyright in the US, the documentation and later
programs, will have to be released into the public domain. I just want a human
reading over this first, and the code, to ensure security and eliminate
redundancies. https://www.mdshare.online/s/fRfg4rbYy4XcWHei4WrhX
[https://www.mdshare.online/s/fRfg4rbYy4XcWHei4WrhX] ### But I’m not getting
paid Neither am I. I can’t even advertise in this app, because of how easy it is
to just go build apps now. Everyone’s complaining about having an alternative to
Reddit. We actually needed one, like yesterday. This is an app the users
control. Which can stay around a while. And, its spec is open from the get-go.
Not by GPL (as I’ve written in the spec), but by public domain, by law! I
literally cannot legally make money from this. It’s not low-effort, so it
doesn’t violate the community rules. But I would love some feedback about things
I haven’t considered. I currently have a massive migraine from all the reading.
